lead.headline: Tate is questionable and 'good to go'; Barkley is out; the lead on paper has halved
lead.deck: Friday's reports are in. Your lineup is still the projection lineup, and the one check is Tate's name on Sunday's inactive list.
lead.body: Start with the bad news about your own players. Carnell Tate practised on a limited basis again on Friday and is listed questionable with the back he tweaked on Thursday. The comfort is second-hand: the Titans' site paraphrases Robert Saleh that Tate 'had tightness' and is 'good to go'. Saquon Barkley is officially out for London, though Philadelphia did not put him on injured reserve, so Week 6 is open. Alvin Kamara is questionable. And your opponent, Kings of the North, has tidied their lineup: Tee Higgins practised in full and is back in their flex, and ESPN's projected margin has halved since this morning, to 133.5 against 122.3, 56%. The good news is banked. George Pickens's 28.0 on Thursday has you ahead 28–1, and CeeDee Lamb's quad turned out to be a bruise, so do not read 13 targets as a new role. Jonathan Taylor practised in full twice. Trevor Lawrence, Bhayshul Tuten and the Jaguars' defence carry no designation for London, where the Eagles will be without Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Hollywood Brown. Chicago's line is cleared for Colston Loveland, and Tyson Bagent starts again. Around the league, Lamar Jackson and Mack Hollins are out and Ashton Jeanty did not practise on Friday. Nothing needs doing today, and no claim: you are last in the order. On Sunday at 09:30, if Tate is inactive, Matthew Golden takes his slot.
